title: Poverty deepens in Bağlar: ‘Many families eat only once a day’
content:
Deepening poverty, rising living costs and difficulties in accessing basic necessities are adversely affecting the living conditions of millions of people in Turkey. According to the Turkish Statistical Institute's (TÜİK) 2025 Poverty and Living Conditions Statistics, 27.9 percent of the population is at risk of poverty or social exclusion. Among children, this figure rises to 36.8 percent.




The same data shows that the material and social deprivation rate stands at 11.9 percent, while the persistent poverty rate is 13.6 percent.




A December 2025 survey by the Confederation of Turkish Trade Unions (TÜRK-İŞ) put the monthly hunger threshold for a family of four at 30,143 Turkish liras and the poverty threshold at 98,188 lira. The net minimum wage of 28,075 liras announced for 2026 falls below the hunger threshold, highlighting the increasingly difficult living conditions.







Deep economic divide between neighbourhoods




As the economic crisis and inflation worsen, millions of people are wondering how they will get through the approaching winter. Residents struggling to cover the costs of natural gas, electricity and firewood say the economic crisis is becoming increasingly severe.

Rather than answering the questions working people raise about its policies, the government attempts to bring them into line by presenting them with another supposed threat.




This mechanism has very concrete consequences. Strikes are postponed on national security grounds. Trade union organising faces repression. Democratic protests are portrayed as security threats. You returned to Qandil after 13 years, once again during a peace process. What changes did you observe over that period? What had remained the same?




If you ask me what remained the same, it was nature. The colours and the light were the same. The natural light in the photographs I took 13 years ago was exactly the same as in the photographs taken this time. Apart from that, 13 years ago, life was lived outdoors. Now, new living spaces have been built inside the mountains, and people live in those spaces. Of course, it is difficult to picture what they are like. Colleagues who had visited before me had told me that they were growing plants inside and so on. But inevitably, you imagine very small, confined spaces and living arrangements that we are not accustomed to. That was not the case at all. They were enormous living spaces.

title: Kurdish and Arab guerrillas pay tribute to commander Bêrîtan, a symbol of freedom for all women
content:
Bêrîtan (Gülnaz Karataş), one of the pioneering commanders of the women’s freedom struggle, was commemorated by Kurdish and Arab women guerrillas on the anniversary of her martyrdom. Drawing attention to Bêrîtan’s spiritual, military, and ideological role, the women guerrillas emphasized that her resistance occupies a historic place in the women’s freedom struggle.




The guerrillas stated that Bêrîtan’s path of resistance has shown all women in the Middle East the way to freedom, adding that her struggle continues to serve as a source of willpower, strength, and inspiration for women today.




Commander Bêrîtan is a symbol of resistance and freedom for all women




Guerrilla Bişenk Brûsk drew attention to the historical impact of Bêrîtan’s actions, stating that her resistance paved the way for the development of women’s military organization.







 







Guerrilla Brûsk said: “Martyr Bêrîtan represents willpower, strength, and morale for us. She was a woman who turned toward her own essence and refused to surrender to the enemy in the face of oppression and hardship. Following her sacrificial act, a women’s military organization developed. She showed us the way to understand both our own reality and the reality of the enemy.”




Bişenk Brûsk also stated that Bêrîtan’s modest and self-sacrificing character continues to be a source of energy and freedom for all her comra

author: Unknown
title: Olive groves of locals seized in Afrin
content:
According to local sources, the Rajo Economic Office seized an olive grove belonging to an 80-year-old woman named Fidan Bilal.




On October 22, the Rajo Economic Office reportedly disregarded the law by bringing workers to Fidan Bilal’s grove and having them harvest the olives for its own benefit.




In the Bilbil district, the Bilbil Economic Office seized resident Ahmed Mamo’s olive grove in the village of Qestel and harvested 28 sacks of olives.




The Bilbil Economic Office stated that the regional director had ordered the seizure of Ahmed Mamo’s grove and prohibited him from harvesting his own olives.




Ahmed Mamo still has 140 olive trees that have yet to be harvested.

title: Journalists march against repression in 10 cities: Without free press, there can be no free society
content:
Numerous press organizations, including the Dicle Fırat Journalists Association (DFG), the Journalists’ Union of Turkey (TGS), DİSK Basın-İş, and the Journalists Association, took to the streets in 10 cities under the slogan “No to censorship! Freedom for news reporting.” A joint press statement was read out in all 10 cities.




The joint statement, titled “Journalism in Turkey means standing with the people, not with those in power, politicians, or capital!”, was read out during the marches and protests, which includes the following:




“As press organizations representing journalists who defend the public’s right to information and pursue the truth, we declare: Enough is enough! We cannot breathe!




We will not remain silent in the face of a system in which journalism is treated as a crime, news reporting as a threat, and the truth as something dangerous; a system in which not only journalists but everyone who raises objections is subjected to censorship, repression, and punishment. There can be no talk of press freedom in a country where trustees are appointed to television channels, news websites are blocked, reporters are arrested, social media accounts are shut down, and journalists are forced to work under conditions resembling slavery while their social rights are stripped away.




Nor can there be any talk of democracy in a country where a media outlet or journali

author: Unknown
title: Saturday Mothers commemorate Hüseyin Toraman
content:
For 35 years, Hüseyin Toraman’s family has been searching for answers about his disappearance in state custody. The then 24-year-old teacher was abducted by armed men in plain clothes outside his apartment in Istanbul 35 years ago. Despite witness statements and an audio recording confirming his detention by the political branch of the Turkish police, his fate remains unknown. At their 1,126th vigil in Istanbul’s Galatasaray Square, the Saturday Mothers commemorated Toraman and demanded that his disappearance be investigated and those responsible be brought to justice.




As they do every Saturday, relatives of the disappeared gathered in Galatasaray Square in the Beyoğlu district, carrying photographs of their abducted and murdered family members and red carnations. The initiative’s statement was read out by Oya Ersoy, Co-Chair of the Human Rights Association (IHD).




Police confirmed detention – investigations yielded no results




On October 27, 1991, Toraman was taken away outside his home in Istanbul’s Kocamustafapaşa district by armed plainclothes men equipped with radios. His wife and several local residents witnessed Toraman being dragged into a white Toros—a reference to the notorious Renault station wagons used by Turkish security forces to abduct, torture, kill, and frequently forcibly disappear numerous opposition figures, particularly in Kurdistan.

title: Communalist students discuss new forms of organizing in Amed
content:
Under the slogan “It is time to unite through communally organized universities,” hundreds of students and young people from Kurdistan and Turkey gathered for a conference in Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır) on Saturday. At the ÇandAmed Congress Center, they discussed the political and social role of youth in the peace and democratic society process, self-organized university structures, and the struggle against social exploitation, environmental destruction, and state repression.




Large portraits of Abdullah Öcalan were displayed in the conference hall, alongside banners bearing slogans such as “The women’s path is the path of life” and “We started young, we will triumph young.” Participants welcomed arriving members of the Peace Mothers Council with a standing ovation. Following a minute of silence, the Kurdish anthem “Çerxa Şoreşê” was sung.




“Youth are the fundamental force in building society”




Hasan Karsu, speaking on behalf of the students, focused his speech on social and ecological crises. In light of the ongoing destruction of nature, particularly in Kurdistan, and growing social insecurity, he called upon young people to take responsibility for creating an alternative way of life. “We must not underestimate the social power that students can generate. We must recognize that young people who develop their own independent will can achieve things beyond our imaginati

author: Unknown
title: YJA Star: We are the inheritors of Bêrîtan’s legacy
content:
The Central Headquarters Command of the Free Women’s Troops (YJA Star) commemorated guerrilla commander Gülnaz Karataş, known by her nom de guerre Bêrîtan Hêvî, highlighting her significance for the Kurdish women’s freedom movement on the 34th anniversary of her death. In a statement on Saturday, YJA Star Command paid tribute to Bêrîtan Hêvî’s resistance against surrender during the Southern War of 1992, describing her political and military legacy as one of the foundations of Kurdish women’s autonomous organization.




Bêrîtan Hêvî was born in 1971 in Bingöl, North Kurdistan, and died on October 25, 1992, in the Xakurke region of South Kurdistan. During clashes between PKK guerrillas and Peshmerga forces allied with the Turkish army, she was surrounded by members of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP). She refused to surrender, fought until her last bullet, destroyed her weapon, and jumped from a cliff to avoid capture.




Her death became an important reference point in the development of autonomous women’s structures within the guerrilla movement. On November 1, 1993, the establishment of a women’s army was announced. YJA Star sees itself as continuing this development and the tradition of resistance among Kurdish women, which it traces from Dersim to the present day.

author: Unknown
title: Democratic Integration Conference in Zurich discusses democratic transformation, equal coexistence
content:
The Kurdish Social Research Association (Akademî Kurd) is holding a conference titled “Democratic Integration” in Zurich, Switzerland. The conference, taking place at the Kirchgemeindehaus, is examining the concept of democratic integration from various perspectives within the framework of LAbdullah Öcalan’s Manifesto for a Democratic Communal Society.




The conference, attended by academics, politicians, legal experts, and researchers, focuses on the theoretical foundations of democratic integration as well as its social, political, and cultural dimensions. Legal reforms necessary for a democratic resolution of the Kurdish question, equal citizenship, the democratic republic, and the democratic communal economy are also among the main topics of discussion.




Dilan Çetinkaya: The process places significant responsibilities on all of us




The conference began with a minute of silence in memory of the martyrs of the revolutionary struggle, followed by an opening speech delivered by Dilan Çetinkaya, Co-Chair of the Democratic Kurdish Council of Switzerland (CDK-S).




Dilan Çetinkaya began her speech by commemorating the martyrs of the Kurdish Freedom Struggle and drew attention to the Kurdish people’s struggle for freedom spanning more than half a century. title: KOMAW calls for international action against death sentence for Varisheh Moradi
content:
The Association of Families of Martyrs and the Disappeared (KOMAW) called on international institutions to intervene against the renewed death sentence imposed on Kurdish activist Varisheh Moradi. In a statement, the organization condemned the Iranian regime’s execution policy and the ongoing repression of women, political activists, and opposition groups. KOMAW has submitted a dossier on Moradi’s case and other human rights violations in Iran to international institutions.




In November 2024, Branch 15 of the Revolutionary Court in Tehran sentenced Moradi to death on charges of “rebellion against the state.” The Supreme Court overturned the ruling in December 2025 due to serious deficiencies in the investigation. Instead of conducting the additional investigations ordered by the Supreme Court, the same court branch once again imposed the death penalty in mid-October. The defense has described the proceedings as unlawful and rejected the accusations against Moradi. The new verdict is not yet final.




KOMAW views the proceedings as another manifestation of the systematic oppression of the Kurdish population in particular, as well as other communities in Iran. “Women who fight for freedom, equality, and democratic rights are particularly vulnerable to persecution and severe punishment. However, human rights must not be sacrificed to political power interests or ideological co

author: Unknown
title: PKK prisoners: We accept neither forced expressions of remorse nor delays in our release
content:
PKK prisoners in Turkish prisons have strongly criticized the continued obstruction of prisoner releases, the practice of forcing prisoners to express remorse, and the lack of political steps in the peace and democratic society process. In a statement signed by Deniz Kaya, they called on the Turkish government to fulfill its responsibility for a democratic resolution of the Kurdish question, remove legal and political obstacles, and create the conditions for the freedom of Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan.




The statement focuses on the decisions of prison Administrative and Observation Boards, which prevent prisoners from being released even after they have served their regular prison sentences. The prisoners particularly reject demands that they renounce their political beliefs or express remorse in order to regain their freedom. They also recall the history of resistance among Kurdish prisoners, particularly in Diyarbakır (Kurdish: Amed) Prison following the military coup of September 12, 1980.




The full statement on Saturday reads as follows:




Delays in the peace process weaken the will to find a solution

author: Unknown
title: Construction Workers' Union, an model for independent unionism
content:
The idea of independent trade unions operating outside the established confederations has long been debated in Turkey. Criticism of existing unions has also led to the establishment of independent organisations in particular sectors.




The debate has been driven by accusations that unions fail to defend workers' rights, cooperate with employers and pay their officials high salaries. Against this backdrop, one union has attracted attention for adopting a different approach.




Founding members killed in massacres




The Construction Workers' Union (Insaat-Is) has distinguished itself through its organising efforts in a sector where trade union activity has historically been limited in Turkey. Operating in the construction industry, which has largely been neglected by trade union confederations, Insaat-Is works in a sector where working conditions make collective bargaining negotiations difficult and maintaining a stable membership has never been possible. Since its official establishment in 2014, the union has become known not only for its trade union struggles but also for its activities in other areas.




The union emerged from discussions and organising efforts prompted by a question raised during a workers' resistance at the Sapphire Tower construction site in 2010: “Why don't construction workers have a union?” The union has also attracted attention for its stance on w

author: Unknown
title: Biçer: Humanitarian and legal steps needed for ill prisoners
content:
Rights violations against sick prisoners continue to increase in prisons. Obstacles to accessing healthcare, delays in hospital transfers and the failure to release seriously ill prisoners are threatening prisoners' right to life.




Sebahat Biçer, an executive of the Federation of Associations for Solidarity with Prisoners' Families (MED TUHAD-FED), spoke to ANF about the rights violations faced by ill prisoners.




‘Urgent steps must be taken regardless of discussions on the peace process’




Sebahat Biçer pointed out that despite ongoing political discussions about the peace process, no concrete progress had been made in prisons. She stressed that releasing sick prisoners was a humanitarian necessity that should not be subject to political bargaining.




Biçer described the lack of progress in prisons and the deep anxiety experienced by prisoners' families: “Yes, that is correct. This peace process has been discussed for more than two years, but so far there has been no progress whatsoever regarding prisons. In fact, regardless of the process, sick prisoners should be released as soon as possible. This is a humanitarian necessity. Yet we have sick prisoners whose coffins could be carried out of prison at any moment. We have prisoners with stage-four cancer. title: Mihemed: We will continue our struggle for constitutional recognition of Kurdish in Syria
content:
Reactions continue in Rojava Kurdistan to the Damascus transitional government's decision concerning the Kurdish language. On 17 October 2026, the Initiative for the Constitutional Recognition of Kurdish and Its Adoption as an Official Language in Syria was announced in Qamishlo. Hesen Mihemed, a member of the initiative, spoke about its activities, aims and objectives.




Hesen Mihemed said there was an urgent need for such an initiative today. He said, “We worked to establish this initiative because our aim was to secure official status for our language. For the past 15 years, students in Rojava have generally been reading, writing and receiving their education in Kurdish, their mother tongue. Unfortunately, under the latest decision, the Syrian Minister of Education has allocated only a few hours, three hours in total, to Kurdish. Even if some other subjects, such as philosophy, mathematics and history, can also be taught in Kurdish, this is unfortunately not enough.




The Kurdish people are an indigenous people, as stated in Article 13 of the Syrian presidential decree. Kurds have rights as Syrian citizens. They must be able to speak, read and receive education in their own language. Unfortunately, however, there has recently been a retreat from these rights. author: Unknown
title: Sevda Karaca: War policies undermine unity and labour struggles - Part One
content:
Sevda Karaca, Deputy Chair of the Labour Party (EMEP) and MP for Antep, answered ANF's questions about labour struggles and the struggle for peace.




Karaca said, “War permeates every aspect of social life. Workers' demands for higher wages, the right to strike, women's struggle for equality and people's democratic demands can suddenly be pushed into the background by debates over 'national security', 'the survival of the state' or the 'domestic front'. The racism, nationalism and chauvinism being fuelled also prevent people, women and young people from coming together around shared demands.”




Karaca stressed that Turkish workers also had a responsibility to oppose the policies of their own ruling classes and support the Kurdish people's demands for peace, equality and democracy. She added, “This is necessary not only as an act of solidarity but also to defend the independent interests of their own class. Because in an environment where peoples are turned against one another, it becomes harder to develop a common struggle against capital.”




How do you assess the current state of the labour struggle in Turkey? Is it sufficient, and where does it fall short?




One of the greatest contradictions in Turkey's labour struggle is this: workers' anger is growing, working and living conditions are deteriorating, and individual pockets of resistance are continuing and spreading

title: Hawari: Syria could lose a century without guaranteed rights
content:
The transitional administration established in Syria following the overthrow of Bashar al-Assad's government faces fundamental challenges, including political legitimacy, economic recovery and the protection of the rights of the country's diverse communities. Journalist and writer Nidal Hawari spoke to ANF about a range of issues, from tensions in Hasakah (Hesekê) and the situation of Alawites and Druze to regional power struggles and strategic straits. He warned that the administration's failure to develop lasting solutions to these problems was increasing uncertainty and deepening social tensions.




Hawari stressed that developments in Syria could not be considered in isolation from one another.




‘The legitimacy of the transitional administration is disputed’




Hawari pointed to the structure of Syria's transitional administration, saying that the current political order had not been established by a government directly elected by the people. He said the way the administration had been formed, from the presidency to the transitional institutions, had raised questions about its legitimacy. He added that the structure established under the leadership of Hayat Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) was not based on a consensus encompassing all communities in the country.

title: YJA Star guerrillas: Martyr Beritan is the embodiment of a free life
content:
Throughout the history of the Kurdish people, there have been many heroic epics that live on in the people’s memory and are never forgotten. Martyr Beritan (Gülnaz Karataş), who shouted in the face of traitors and became a symbol of resistance and the free woman’s stance, represented the essence of the Kurdish woman.




Hesret Dilgeş Amed, one of the YJA Star commanders, spoke about martyr Beritan’s actions and resistance. Beginning her remarks by commemorating martyr Beritan and the martyrs of October.







 







Hesret Dilgeş Amed said: “Comrade Beritan joined the ranks of the freedom movement in the 1990s, at a time when the Kurdish people were rising up throughout Kurdistan. Comrade Beritan came to know Leader Apo by reading his books and studying his analyses. She organized her life through the knowledge she gained from Abdullah Öcalan and through her own efforts.




At that time, there were also liquidationists within our movement who wanted to dismantle it. Through her stance in life, her organizational commitment, and her free will, Comrade Beritan stood against these liquidationists. In this way, she upheld Öcalan’s line. Martyr Beritan put Öcalan’s ideas into practice in her own life. For this reason, no force could intimidate her or break her resolve.

author: Unknown
title: Slovenian philosopher Slavoj Žižek writes letter to Öcalan
content:
Slavoj Žižek, a Slovenian philosopher and one of the leading figures in Marxist thought, wrote a letter to Abdullah Öcalan. The letter, which Žižek sent to the Imralı delegation, reads as follows:




“Dear Abdullah Öcalan,




Today, there are leaders whom we feel compelled to support only because they represent the least bad option among two or three bad choices. However, choosing between bad options never brings a solution; it merely produces a compromise that carries within itself the seeds of its own failure.




You are one of the very few leaders who can and should be supported unconditionally. This is because you combine a principled stance and a profound, theory-based approach with sound pragmatism and a willingness to make difficult decisions.




You are fully aware that the struggle you are waging for the Kurds is not a struggle against the Turks. If you succeed, it will not be only the Kurds who benefit; both sides will win. All citizens of Turkey will enjoy greater freedom, peace, and prosperity.”

title: Öcalan’s book ‘Manifesto of the Democratic Communal Society’ banned in prison
content:
The administration of Siverek No. 1 T-Type Closed Prison in Urfa has prohibited political prisoner Tacittin Kalgı from receiving the book 

Manifesto of the Democratic Communal Society

. The decision was justified on the grounds that the book allegedly contains material posing a threat to security. DEM Party MP Newroz Uysal Aslan has therefore appealed to the Human Rights Commission of the Turkish Parliament, calling for an investigation into the ban.




The measure is based on a decision issued by the prison administration on October 8, under file number 2026/390. The decision specifically objects to passages addressing the historical and political dimensions of the Kurdish question, Abdullah Öcalan’s ideas, the history of the Kurdish movement, and the paradigm of a democratic society.




The prison’s Education Board maintains that the book damages the reputation of the state, contains terrorist propaganda, and could incite hatred and hostility.




Even Öcalan’s call for peace is deemed objectionable




In her petition, Uysal Aslan pointed out that even passages concerning Öcalan’s February 27, 2025, Call for Peace and Democratic Society were deemed objectionable. The book addresses, among other issues, the transition from armed struggle to democratic politics and perspectives on coexistence within society.

title: Three dead and two missing after flooding in Urmia
content:
At least three people have died in severe flooding in Urmia province in Rojhilat (Eastern Kurdistan). Two others remain missing, while six people have been injured. Heavy rainfall and hailstorms triggered flash floods, particularly in the northern part of the province. The districts of Selmas and Maku have been hardest hit.




According to the provincial Red Crescent Directorate in Urmia, the fatalities occurred in the village of Kaniyan near Selmas, where flooding intensified significantly overnight. Following an extensive search, rescue teams recovered three bodies, including those of a ten-year-old girl and a 63-year-old man. The search for two other missing people is ongoing.




Severe damage to homes and infrastructure




The floodwaters caused extensive damage to homes, roads, and utility infrastructure, particularly in rural areas. According to preliminary assessments, at least 25 houses were flooded and partially destroyed. Eleven vehicles became stranded in floodwaters on connecting roads and near villages.




Search and rescue teams were dispatched to the affected areas. Residents of several flooded villages had to evacuate their homes and were moved to safety.

title: More than 70 Kurdish families face displacement in Kirkuk
content:
Demolition work for a planned housing development began on Thursday in the Kurdish village of Aliawa in Kirkuk province. More than 70 families face the destruction of their homes and the threat of displacement once again. Residents are protesting the authorities’ actions, pointing out that the land was officially allocated to them years ago.




The village is located on the main road between Kirkuk and Dibis, northwest of the provincial capital. According to local media reports, construction machinery arrived on Thursday and began demolishing shops and commercial premises. More than 70 residential buildings are expected to be demolished in a subsequent phase. Residents say that between 70 and 80 Kurdish families are affected.




‘Now they want to displace us again’




The residents are internally displaced people from Kirkuk who were officially resettled in Aliawa in 2011 and 2012 under Article 140 of the Iraqi Constitution. The constitutional provision calls for the normalization of conditions in disputed territories and the resolution of their political status.




“These plots of land were officially allocated to us by the Commission for Displaced Persons. Now they want to drive us out without any regard for our rights, through political interference. This means we are being displaced once again,” a villager said.

author: Unknown
title: Shengal delegation holds talks at the European Parliament
content:
A diplomatic delegation from Shengal visited the European Parliament in Strasbourg to raise awareness of the situation facing the Yazidi population and the threats to the region. The discussions focused on conditions in Şengal and the challenges confronting its people.




The delegation included Azad Hisên, co-chair of the Shengal People’s Council; Sara Şengalî, a member of the Jineolojî Committee; and Kurdish politician and former Member of the European Parliament Feleknas Uca.




During their visit, the delegation members met with representatives of various political groups and parties in the European Parliament. Those they met included Swedish MEP Jonas Sjöstedt of The Left group, Austrian MEP Andreas Schieder (SPÖ), Galician MEP Ana Miranda Paz, and German MEPs Katrin Langensiepen (Greens), Martin Schirdewan (Die Linke), and Özlem Alev Demirel, also of Die Linke.

content:

Legal reforms and a democratic communal economy will also be among the main topics of discussion, particularly in relation to a democratic solution to the Kurdish question.

Political, sociological and cultural dimensions to be discussed




The conference’s second session, scheduled for 11 a.m. to 1 p.m., will focus on “The Political, Sociological, and Cultural Dimensions of Democratic Integration.”

title: Imprisoned PKK members commemorate martyrs and reaffirm commitment to peace
content:
PKK prisoners incarcerated in Turkey issued a joint statement commemorating those who lost their lives in the Kurdish freedom struggle and reaffirming their determination to carry forward their legacy through the Peace and Democratic Society Process. In the statement released by Deniz Kaya, they emphasized that remembering the martyrs is inseparably linked to the pursuit of a democratic resolution to the Kurdish question.




The statement followed the publication of the identities of members of the Kurdish freedom movement who lost their lives at different times and in various areas of resistance. The prisoners paid tribute to their fallen comrades and all those who lost their lives in the struggle for freedom and democracy.




“The martyrs embody the historical memory of our struggle, its ideological core, and the deepest truth of our pursuit of freedom,” the statement said.




It added that each individual’s life and struggle formed part of the collective aspiration for a free life, the determination to resist, and the hope for a democratic future.




Embedding peace in society




The statement underlined that: "Commemoration means not only keeping the past alive in collective memory but also taking responsibility for the future. Honoring the martyrs must be reflected in political attitudes, the assumption of social responsibility, and organizational renewal."

author: Unknown
title: Özbingöl: Government politicians must act responsibly for peace
content:
The recognition of Kurdish People's Leader Abdullah Öcalan's political status as the chief negotiator and the provision of conditions enabling him to work freely are among the key demands for advancing the Peace and Democratic Society Process. However, successive statements on the issue by Mehmet Uçum, Chief Adviser to the President and Deputy Chair of the Presidential Legal Policies Board, have sparked criticism.




Uçum, who has reduced the question of Kurdish People's Leader Abdullah Öcalan's status to the issue of disarmament, claimed that raising demands such as Öcalan's release was obstructing the process. His remarks have drawn criticism for disregarding the historical and political dimensions of the problems arising from the denial of Kurdish identity. 




Uçum also made the following remarks on discussions surrounding a new constitution: “The advancement of democracy and the adoption of a new constitution will only become matters for the entire nation to address and implement once the transition to a Terror-Free Turkey has been completed, ethnic and identity politics have been left behind, and the issues associated with them have been resolved not only in practice but also in people's minds. title: Resistance against solar power plant project kicks off in Amed
content:
Resistance against the planned “Zenkar 2 Solar Power Plant and Energy Storage Facility” project in Amed’s Arzoxlî neighborhood entered its second day. While legal proceedings against the project’s “Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Positive” decision are ongoing, company employees entered the construction site accompanied by the gendarmerie and riot police.




In response, neighborhood residents, representatives of political parties and civil society organizations, and environmental activists marched to the project site. A banner reading “Our ancient city of Ğırap and our village must not be sacrificed to capital” was unfurled, while protesters chanted, “Our land, our water, our existence.”




Prevented from accessing fields




Residents encountered a gendarmerie blockade near the project site and demanded an explanation of the legal basis for the work being carried out in the area. Lawyer Ahmet İnan, chair of the Environment and Urban Affairs Commission of the Amed Bar Association, said the restrictions were not limited to the project site and that access to fields outside the construction area was also being blocked.




Berdan Öztürk, a DEM Party member of parliament for Amed, said they opposed the project, stating that villagers were being deprived of their right to life and that people were being forced to leave the places where they lived.

content:
The General Command of the Women’s Protection Units (YPJ) issued a statement to condemn the death sentence re-issued against Varisheh Moradi. The statement said:

 "

The Islamic regime in Iran’s issuance of a death sentence against Kurdish activist and political prisoner Varisheh Moradi reflects the expansion of the policy of femicide and constitutes a direct attack on the will and aspirations for freedom of all women.




The history of the Iranian regime demonstrates that this reactionary authority has consistently sought to suppress the resistance of the Kurdish people and women’s struggle for liberation through executions and the spread of fear. From Shirin Alam-Houli to Zeynab Jalalian, and now Varisheh Moradi, the repression of women who resist has remained deeply rooted in the mindset of this authority. Fearing the philosophy and slogan “Woman, Life, Freedom”, this regime is once again attempting, through these inhumane sentences, to take revenge on the legacy of resistance and the pioneers of the women’s struggle. Yet history has repeatedly proved that policies of intimidation and executions cannot break the will of women who have risen up for freedom."

author: Unknown
title: Aydın: Peace process cannot be reduced to disarmament
content:
As discussions over the peace process continue in Turkey, Cihan Aydın, Co-Chair of the Human Rights Association (IHD), assessed the current stage of the process and the shortcomings of the legal measures introduced so far. Aydın said the state must take responsibility for democratisation if lasting peace is to be achieved.




Aydın warned that the process would remain fragile unless steps towards disarmament were accompanied by measures to strengthen fundamental rights and freedoms. He stressed that the steps taken since the beginning of the process were important, but that the legal framework still contained significant shortcomings.




Aydın said the process had been under way for more than two years. He pointed to statements by the government and Devlet Bahçeli, followed by the Kurdish People's Leader Abdullah Öcalan's declaration on 27 February. He described the subsequent mutual expressions of goodwill and the steps taken by the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) towards laying down its arms and dissolving itself as important milestones.




Aydın said the law adopted at the current stage contained significant shortcomings. He noted that it focused primarily on disarmament and offered no guarantees or commitments concerning democratisation or the fundamental rights and freedoms of Kurds. title: SGDF member Usta: I was abducted, tortured and forced to become an informant
content:
Hasan Basri Usta, a member of the Federation of Socialist Youth Associations (SGDF), said he was forced into a vehicle by individuals who identified themselves as police officers while returning home in Ankara's Dikimevi neighbourhood on the evening of 15 October. Usta said he was beaten inside the vehicle, that his abductors attempted to unlock his phone using his fingerprint and that he was pressured to provide information about people he was involved in political activism with.




Usta told 

Bianet

 that he was subjected to violence and threats for approximately three hours before being taken out of the vehicle blindfolded in an isolated, mountainous area of Ankara's Mamak district. He will file a criminal complaint

title: Fırat: Cem Foundation seeks to appoint trustee to Kıraç Cemevi
content:

The eviction has been postponed for one month. Those demanding the complete cancellation of the transfer decision are determined to continue their vigil outside the cemevi until their demand is met. ‘The walls of this cemevi were built through the people's labour!’




Celal Fırat, MP for the DEM Party, brought the decision to transfer Kıraç Cemevi to the Cem Foundation on the grounds that it stands on Treasury-owned land before parliament and met with the Interior Minister to seek its cancellation. Fırat stressed that the cemevi had been built over the years through the collective efforts of the Alevi community.

title: Political prisoner Ali Adıman’s release postponed by six years for using the phrase ‘Mr. Öcalan’
content:
Newroz Uysal Aslan, an MP of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) for Şırnak province, submitted a parliamentary question to Justice Minister Akın Gürlek, stating that political prisoners’ rights to freedom of expression and to submit petitions are being violated through disciplinary sanctions in prisons.




The parliamentary question stated that solitary confinement penalties imposed on Ali Adıman, who is held in Bolu F-Type Prison, for using the phrase “Mr. Öcalan” in a petition sent to the Ministry of Justice had been used as grounds to postpone his release by six years.




In her parliamentary question, Newroz Uysal Aslan asked what legal basis justified imposing disciplinary sanctions on prisoners and postponing their release for using a form of address that, she argued, does not constitute a criminal offense. She also raised the question of whether decisions made by prison administrations could take precedence over the constitution, laws, and rulings of higher courts.




The MP demanded information on how many prisoners had received solitary confinement penalties for using the phrase “Mr. Öcalan,” how many had been prevented from being released, and how many appeals against these decisions had been resolved.

author: Unknown
title: DEM Party criticizes the government over the process: Why are steps toward peace being delayed?
content:
The Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) spokesperson Ayşegül Doğan assessed the progress of the Peace and Democratic Society Process at a press conference following her party’s Central Executive Committee (MYK) meeting. Stating that the process was being delayed, Doğan said uncertainties surrounding democratization and legal reforms persisted despite statements from the government.







 










When will Abdullah Öcalan’s conditions be changed?




Recalling the call made by Nationalist Movement Party (MHP) leader Devlet Bahçeli in parliament on October 22, 2024, Ayşegül Doğan stated that no significant changes had been made to Öcalan’s conditions since then, apart from visits by the DEM Party’s Imrali delegation.




Doğan noted that family visits had not been placed on a regular schedule either.




“Since the call made on October 22, 2024, changes to Mr. Öcalan’s conditions have been limited to visits by the DEM Party’s Imrali delegation. Family visits are taking place, but there is no regular schedule for them. So, as a political party that frequently seeks answers to this question, we ask: When will these conditions change?”




Who is delaying the process?




Emphasizing that reciprocal steps are necessary for the process to move forward, Doğan recalled that the PKK had declared a ceasefire, convened its congress and announced its decision to dissolve

author: Unknown
title: Altun: We must dedicate 24 hours a day to Abdullah Öcalan’s freedom
content:
Kenan Altun, who had been imprisoned for 30 years, was released from Maltepe No. 1 L-Type Prison. Welcomed outside the prison, Altun said, “We have been released after 30 years, but Abdullah Öcalan is still inside. If we do not dedicate our 24 hours to Abdullah Öcalan’s freedom, we will not achieve results.”







 







Altun also delivered the following message: “All our friends send their greetings. On their behalf and my own, I thank you for welcoming me. Many of our friends inside are ill. I have just left behind a friend who is 84 years old and still in prison. Nevertheless, both I and all our friends are in very high spirits. They all send you their warmest greetings.




All our people must work together and dedicate our 24 hours to peace. We know that the burden we carry is very heavy. This is not a time to sit back; on the contrary, it is a time to intensify the struggle. For all the sacrifices we have made, for our future, and for our children, we must dedicate our 24 hours to the struggle.”

title: DBP engages with the public on peace: ‘We will develop a roadmap’
content:
The Democratic Regions Party (DBP) is holding public meetings in various cities under the slogan “Building the language of peace together with the people” to promote broader public participation in the peace and resolution process. The meetings, attended by party leaders, co-chairs, members of the Central Executive Committee (MYK), and Party Council members, are continuing across numerous cities in Kurdistan.




Aiming to reach a broad cross-section of society, from workers and civil society organizations to different faith communities and political groups, the DBP seeks to listen to the public’s expectations and proposals during these meetings and develop new policies concerning the process.




‘We aim to reach all segments of society through these meetings’




Speaking to ANF on the scope of the initiative, DBP Party Council member Bünyamin Şeker emphasized that the public meetings go beyond simply organizing gatherings. The activities are not limited to a single day, but involve extensive programs held across different parts of each city. Through these programs, the party aims to reach all segments of society and shape the discourse on peace together with the people.




Şeker pointed out that the primary objective of the public meetings is to help society understand the process, adding that the party has been working toward this goal since the February 27 declaration.

title: Ruşen Yakut: Policies of impunity in femicide cases must end
content:
According to Ruşen Yakut of the Rosa Women’s Association, the growing number of femicides in Turkey and Kurdistan reflects a systematic, patriarchal structure of violence. Militarization, state repression, and impunity for perpetrators are exacerbating the situation, while state protection mechanisms frequently fail. In an interview with ANF, Yakut calls for a fundamental shift in policies concerning women, Turkey’s return to the Istanbul Convention, and the consistent criminal prosecution of violence against women.




“We are living through a period in which femicides are increasing dramatically. This violence has now reached the scale of systematic femicide,” Yakut said.




She identifies the patriarchal system itself as the root cause: “Militarism, which underpins nation-state structures, the growing emphasis on security, and the strengthening of sexist policies worldwide are further fueling violence against women.”




Yakut argues that the Turkish government’s policies are shaped by an authoritarian, nationalist, and sexist vision of society that undermines fundamental freedoms and social diversity. At the same time, the economic crisis, the growing prevalence of privately owned firearms, and the political climate are exacerbating violence.

title: TJA stages torchlight marches in Istanbul for Öcalan’s freedom
content:
The Free Women’s Movement (Tevgera Jinên Azad, TJA) held simultaneous torchlight marches in three Istanbul districts, demanding an end to Abdullah Öcalan’s isolation and his physical freedom. The demonstrations in Küçükçekmece, Gaziosmanpaşa, and Sancaktepe also called on the Turkish government and parliament to establish the legal and political conditions necessary for lasting peace. Police blocked the marches in all three districts.




Alongside numerous women, representatives of political parties and civil society organizations also took part in the demonstrations. Participants lit torches and unfurled banners bearing slogans such as “Now Is the Time to Win – Time to Meet the Free Leader” and “Now Is the Time for Women.” They also chanted slogans including “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” [Woman, Life, Freedom], “Bijî Serok Apo” [Long Live Leader Öcalan], and “A Thousand Greetings to Imrali.”




In Gaziosmanpaşa, police prevented the planned march from taking place at Karayolları Square. Gatherings in Küçükçekmece and Sancaktepe were also blocked by police barricades. Participants protested the police intervention by chanting slogans.

“Mr. Öcalan’s vision of a democratic society has created an important historical foundation for ending conflicts and strengthening democratic politics, both in the Middle East and in Turkey,” the declaration said.




Call to intensify the struggle for freedom, equality, and peace

title: Where are the Zapatistas 30 years later?
content:
The Zapatista Army of National Liberation (EZLN – Ejército Zapatista de Liberación Nacional), which emerged in Chiapas in the first days of 1994, came to the world's attention through an armed uprising in a region of Mexico marked by widespread poverty and inequality, where Indigenous people make up a significant proportion of the population. However, it was not only the uprising that made the Zapatista experience distinctive.




In the years that followed, the movement moved away from the goal of seizing state power and developed a practice of autonomy centred on the right of Indigenous communities to govern themselves. In this direction, it established autonomous governance, education, healthcare and production structures based on local communities. Over more than thirty years, as demands for Indigenous rights and political autonomy were not sufficiently realised, the Zapatistas declared their own autonomous governance structures and reorganised them several times. Having established autonomous municipalities and regional administrative centres for a period, the movement dissolved these structures in 2023, shifting decision-making processes to a model based on smaller, local communities.

title: Thousands commemorate 69 fallen guerrilla fighters in Kobanê
content:
Thousands of people from various cities across Rojava gathered in Kobanê to commemorate 69 members of the People’s Defense Forces (HPG) and the Free Women’s Troops (YJA Star) who lost their lives in the Kurdish freedom struggle over the years. Relatives of the fallen fighters, along with representatives of political parties and civil society organizations, attended the commemoration at the Şehîd Dicle Cemetery. The ceremony began with a minute of silence, followed by the reading of the names of the 69 guerrilla fighters.




Mustafa Êto, co-chair of the Council of War Veterans and Families of the Martyrs in Kobanê, paid tribute to the deceased fighters’ commitment to a democratic and just society.




“Our martyrs waged a historic struggle under all circumstances. Sixty-nine names also mean sixty-nine mothers. We will remain committed to their cause until the end,” he declared.

title: Iran strikes Kurdistan National Army headquarters in Hewler countryside
content: The Kurdistan Freedom Party (Partiya Azadiya Kurdistanê – PAK) announced that Iran had bombarded the Kurdistan National Army base in the Herîr-Balîsan area of Hewlêr with ballistic missiles. title: Ulus: Healthcare must be free and accessible to all
content:
Structural problems in public hospitals and shortcomings in healthcare services are making it increasingly difficult for citizens to access medical care. People struggling to secure appointments through the Central Physician Appointment System (MHRS) sometimes have to wait at least 15 days just to submit an appointment request. Patients who eventually manage to obtain appointments after considerable effort must then try to explain their health problems within limited consultation times due to overcrowding in hospitals.




Difficulties in securing appointments and restrictions on consultation times are further deepening problems concerning the quality and accessibility of healthcare services.




Mehmet Nuri Ulus, Co-Chair of the Diyarbakır (Amed) Branch of the Health and Social Service Workers’ Union (SES), spoke to ANF about the problems facing public hospitals.




‘Healthcare is not being transformed, it is going backwards’




Ulus recalled that the Justice and Development Party (AKP) government has introduced healthcare reform and transformation programmes since 2002. title: HANA: Iranian regime abducts and disappears Kurds
content:
The HANA Human Rights Organization has published a report on the arrest and abduction of Kurds by the Iranian regime.




According to the report, Diyako Bayezîdî and Mustafa Coşkar, both from Mahabad, were detained by the Iranian regime’s intelligence forces in the city and taken to an undisclosed location. The report also stated that 17-year-old Îlya Lutfî Tormakçî, who lives in the city of Baneh, was abducted by masked forces affiliated with the Iranian regime.




The report further noted that 19-year-old Ehed Meyhenxahî, from the Shino district of Urmia, was arrested on 19 October and transferred to Naghadeh Prison following a five-year prison sentence imposed on him.




Ehed Meyhenxahî had previously been detained by Iran’s Ministry of Intelligence (Ettelaat) on 24 January 2026, without a prosecutorial order, and was released on bail approximately one month later. He was subsequently sentenced to prison by the Shino Revolutionary Court on charges of “assisting anti-Iran opposition.”




The Hana Human Rights Organization’s report also stated that on 16 October, intelligence forces of the Iranian regime raided the home of Aram Eminî in Saqqez and abducted him without a written warrant or a prosecutorial order. The report said that, despite five days having passed, no information was yet available regarding Aram Eminî’s whereabouts.

title: Diyarbakır Bar Association: 568 rights violations against children recorded in six months
content:
The Diyarbakır Bar Association’s Children’s Rights Center compiled reports of children’s rights violations that came to public attention during the first six months of the year. According to the report, a total of 344 children lost their lives during this six-month period. Of these children, 326 died from preventable causes, while 18 died under suspicious circumstances.




A total of 224 children were involved in cases involving sexual offenses, violence, and grievous bodily harm, while the total number of children affected by violations of the right to life and other forms of victimization was recorded at 568.




Recommendations




The report outlined the following structural and legal recommendations:




- School Security, Public Safety in Surrounding Areas, and Disarmament: Physical inspections and X-ray barriers should be installed to prevent weapons such as smooth bore hunting rifles and knives from being brought into educational institutions. Criminal penalties for civilian gun ownership should be increased.




- MESEM Programs Should Be Suspended: MESEM programs, which place children in heavy and hazardous occupations, should be suspended. Industrial facilities and construction sites should be inspected by independent, multi-stakeholder monitoring boards.

author: Unknown
title: Iran builds wall along border between South Kurdistan and Rojhilat
content:
According to RojNews, Iranian forces have built a 10-kilometer-long concrete wall stretching from the Seyranben Border Crossing on the border between Bashur (South Kurdistan) and Rojhilat (East Kurdistan) to an area behind the villages of Teymiz and Şêweguwêzan. Observation towers have also been constructed along the wall.




It was further reported that trenches measuring 3 meters wide and 4 meters deep have been dug along the borderline extending from the wall to the village of Mîşyawe, and that strict security measures have been imposed along the border.







 







Iran had previously sought to sever connections between Bashur and Rojhilat by laying barbed wire and landmines along the border. These efforts are now reportedly continuing through the construction of walls and trenches along the border between the two regions.




The construction of the wall and trenches is particularly noteworthy because it is taking place at a time when Iraqi Border Guard forces have been deployed along the borders and forces at border checkpoints belonging to both countries are engaged in dialogue.




Despite Iraqi and Iranian officials repeatedly emphasizing security coordination between Iran, Iraq, and the Kurdistan Region, the Iranian and Iraqi governments have chosen to remain silent about the reasons behind the construction of the wall and the digging of the trenches.

The journal of the Academy of Social Science, 

Democratic Modernity

Towards a Sociology of Freedom

The journal critiques capitalism, hierarchical institutions, and conventional disciplinary boundaries, advocating instead for forms of social organization grounded in communal life, dignity, ecological awareness, and democratic participation.




The journal combines essays on political theory, sociology, art, food systems, jineolojî, knowledge, and community organizing. The journal will also be the address where the fruit of research communes such as

title: Two women killed in Sulaymaniyah and Mardin
content:
Two women have died in Sulaymaniyah in South Kurdistan and in Mardin in North Kurdistan. Kîjan Bûrhan was shot by her father and succumbed to her severe injuries, while Remziye Damar was found dead in her home under unexplained circumstances.




Kîjan Bûrhan was shot by her father in Sulaymaniyah on Monday evening. The 30-year-old woman was struck by three bullets. She was taken for medical treatment in critical condition but died from her injuries on Tuesday afternoon.




Meanwhile, Remziye Damar was found lifeless in her home in the village of Boxazîyê in Kızıltepe district. Emergency services arrived following a call for assistance and confirmed her death. Her body was taken to the forensic medicine department of Kızıltepe State Hospital for an autopsy. Following the completion of the examinations, Damar was laid to rest in her home village of Boxazîyê.

In a visual message featuring numerous AbM members, the movement called on the Iranian regime to end its policies of repression and executions targeting Kurds. The message demanded the immediate release of Varisheh Moradi and all other political prisoners, while expressing solidarity with the women’s freedom struggle in Kurdistan through the slogan “Jin Jiyan Azadî” (Woman, Life, Freedom).

title: Mechthild Exo: Jineolojî must become a lived foundation
content:
Twelve years after the first Jineolojî conference in Europe, Kurdish women’s science has established itself in numerous countries. However, its integration into society continues to face significant challenges. Peace and conflict researcher Dr. Mechthild Exo highlighted these issues on the sidelines of the latest Jineolojî conference. In an interview with ANF, she traces the development of academic and feminist work since 2014 and explains why research, political organizing, and social practice must become more closely interconnected in the future.




When the first European Jineolojî conference took place in Cologne in 2014, those involved were still at the very beginning of their work, Exo noted. There were no established structures, extensive educational programs, or sufficient translations of foundational literature. Jineolojî, which defines itself as the science of women and life and emerged from the Kurdish women’s freedom movement, first had to be introduced, explained, and made accessible, Exo stated.




“We didn’t really know what Jineolojî was. We only knew that a new science was being developed,” Exo said. "The first conference was largely characterized by a collective search for understanding. content:

title: Sermin Demirdağ’s release delayed for the eighth time
content:
The release of Sermin Demirdağ, who is being held at Kayseri Women’s Closed Prison, has been postponed for six months for the eighth time by the Prison Administration and Observation Board.




Sermin Demirdağ, who has been imprisoned since 13 April 1993, had previously had her release postponed seven times through board decisions at Sincan Women’s Closed Prison, where she was formerly held.




With this latest decision, the total time added to Sermin Demirdağ’s imprisonment has reached four years and three months, as her release has been blocked since 7 March 2023.

title: Kalkan: The legal and political groundwork for Öcalan’s physical freedom must now be established
content:
Duran Kalkan, a member of the Abdullah Öcalan Academy of Social Sciences, gave an interview to Medya Haber TV, sharing his assessment on the recent developments.




This is an excerpt of the interview. 




You have assessed the past two years of the process. There is also the situation in the prisons. While the release of prisoners under a framework law is being discussed, we see that even those who have served their sentences are not being released. There is complete arbitrariness here. This seems to have sparked serious debate and anger within society…




What I have said applies here as well. Turkey's laws are, in fact, subject to oversight by the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR). Its rulings must be implemented. Yet none of them are being implemented. Under the current Justice and Development Party (AKP) government, Turkey is enforcing neither its own constitution nor its criminal laws. They have now set up some sort of committee, whose members are not even legal professionals. They have brought together prison guards and people from here and there, and these committees decide whether prisoners are released. It is not the law that decides. It is not the courts that decide.

title: Freedom guerrillas: We will uphold women martyrs’ legacy of resistance
content:
Freedom guerrillas commemorated pioneering women martyrs, highlighting the significance of October in the history of their struggle. People's Defence Forces (HPG) guerrilla Cumali Ararat emphasised the legacy of struggle left by Azime, Canda, Ronahî (Andrea Wolf) and Berîtan (Gülnaz Karataş), saying that the women's liberation movement has gained support around the world.




Cumali Ararat said that October holds particular significance in the history of women's military organisation and the tradition of resistance.







 







He reflected on the month's place in the history of their struggle and said: “Every month has its own significance in our life of struggle. October is also a meaningful month in the history of our struggle and women's military organisation. It is a month of resistance. Looking back at history, we see that our women comrades played a pioneering role and fulfilled a leading mission in the tradition of struggle during this significant month. For example, there were comrades Azime, Canda and Ronahî the German. Comrade Ronahî was an internationalist. Abdullah Öcalan's ideas and philosophy had a profound influence on her. Comrade Ronahî refused to surrender to the enemy and was martyred when the enemy riddled her body with bullets.




October is also associated with our comrade Berîtan, a pioneering commander in women's military organisation and a symbol

author: Unknown
title: Democratisation is not about imposing conditions
content:
Mehmet Uçum (Chief Adviser to the President and Deputy Chair of the Presidential Legal Policies Board) wrote an article about the process on 17 October. Judging by his remarks, Uçum appears to be acting as the spokesperson for a group seeking to undermine the process. He claims to advocate dialogue, yet he is trying to dictate terms to the Kurdish Freedom Movement. He seems to think he is intelligent and everyone else is a fool. The article Uçum wrote is precisely the kind of article that opponents of the process, those seeking to sabotage it, would write. If it reflects the views of Tayyip Erdoğan, whom he advises, the situation is even more serious and troubling. If that is the case, the government is attempting to lay the ideological groundwork for undermining the process. Tayyip Erdoğan has repeatedly said that the process is progressing well. If Mehmet Uçum wrote his article based on information received from the presidential palace, it means the process is not going well.




Even before the law approved on 18 August was enacted, government officials had said that the status of Kurdish People's Leader Abdullah Öcalan would change, that he would meet with various groups and that even those who would work alongside him would be able to visit Imrali. These commitments were made before the law was passed. Following its enactment, the deputy chair of the Justice and Developmen

title: Zübeyir Aydar: Kurds have the right to speak at the UN
content:
The Kurds' struggle for international recognition and representation is entering a new phase. Zübeyir Aydar, a member of the Executive Council of the Kurdistan National Congress (KNK), said that despite their population of approximately 60 million, Kurds are not represented internationally through their own political will. Aydar said, “We also want to be represented. Our demand is equality.”




Aydar spoke to ANF and emphasised that the initiative to secure representation at the United Nations (UN) is not merely a diplomatic demand but an important part of the Kurds' struggle for recognition as an equal people.




We spoke to Zübeyir Aydar, a member of the Executive Council of the KNK, about the demands raised and decisions taken at the conference organised by the KNK in Brussels on 3 October, as well as the importance of Kurdish national unity.




What challenges do Kurds face today in terms of international recognition and representation?




As a people and a nation, we are not officially recognised. Our struggle is for the Kurds to be recognised by everyone, just like other nations around the world. Yes, the existence of the Kurds is acknowledged, and Kurds are recognised, but this recognition has not yet acquired the legal, political and diplomatic status we seek.




There has been official recognition in Iraq since 2004. Kurds have federal status within Iraq. In Syria

title: Commemoration in Kobanê for 68 martyrs
content:
A tent has been erected at Martyr Dicle Cemetery in Kobanê to commemorate 68 YJA Star/HPG guerrillas who fell as martyrs in different years while serving in the ranks of the Kurdistan Freedom Movement.




On Tuesday, a convoy of people from the cities and towns of Til Temir, Hesekê, Zirgan, Dirbêsiyê, Qamişlo, Dêrik, Girkê Legê, Til Koçer, Amûdê, Tirbespiyê and Çilaxa gathered at the Kandil Junction in Til Temir before setting off for Kobanê to attend the ceremony.




In observance of the commemoration, all shops and markets in the city of Kobanê were closed.




According to information provided by the Council of Martyrs’ Families, speeches will be delivered at the ceremony on behalf of the Council of Martyrs’ Families, the Kongra Star Coordination, political parties, the Democratic Islam Congress and numerous other organizations.




In addition, a video message from Murat Karayılan, central commander of the People's Defense Headquarter, will be shown. A video presentation documenting the lives, struggle and sacrifices of the fallen fighters will also be screened.

title: Submission to the Council of Europe: ECtHR ruling on Öcalan remains unimplemented after 12 years
content:
According to Mezopotamya Agency (MA), Asrın Law Office, which represents Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan, submitted a communication to the Council of Europe’s Committee of Ministers over Turkey’s failure to implement the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) ruling issued in 2014.




The submission recalled the Committee of Ministers’ interim resolution of September 17, 2025, concerning the Gurban group of cases, which includes the “Öcalan No. 2” judgment.




It noted that the Committee had requested information from Turkey by the end of June 2026 on progress made in implementing the judgments, but that Turkey had failed to submit the required information or an action plan within that period.




The law office stated that Turkey had not established any legal mechanism allowing aggravated life sentences to be reviewed after a specified period.




Öcalan excluded from the scope of the legislation




The submission also addressed the bill on 

Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Cohesion

. Prepared as part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, the bill was submitted to the Parliamentary Speaker’s Office on 5 August and subsequently passed by Parliament’s Justice Commission. It was also debated in the General Assembly and adopted with 468 votes.

title: Meral Çiçek: Jineology must develop concrete solutions to social problems
content:
Journalist Meral Çiçek, who attended the European Jineology Conference in Haelen, the Netherlands, spoke to ANF about the educational activities carried out across Europe over the past decade, the key discussions at the conference and the work that needs to be developed in the coming period.




Meral Çiçek said that Jineology has brought about significant changes in women's approaches to knowledge and learning. She stressed that, in the coming period, research into social problems must go hand in hand with the development of solutions. She also highlighted the importance of strengthening ties and developing joint projects with women's organisations.







 







‘Knowledge is hidden in every aspect of life’




Meral Çiçek highlighted the methodological diversity of Jineology's educational activities in Europe, conducted through camps, seminars, workshops and conferences. She said these activities have encouraged women to develop new ways of questioning and examining the world around them.




Çiçek explained that education is not regarded merely as the transmission of knowledge, emphasising that Jineology encourages women to question existing knowledge while also transforming their understanding of where knowledge comes from.

author: Unknown
title: Whereabouts of five people detained by Iranian forces unknown
content:
A report published by Kolbernews provided information about the disappearance of five mountaineers from Rojhilat (East Kurdistan) following their detention by Iranian state forces.




More than 30 armed Iranian intelligence agents reportedly raided the homes of seven members of the Helo and Sewz Mountain groups, independent mountaineering groups based in Saqqez. The mountaineers were detained following the home raids.




The report stated that the mountaineers Abdullah Amini and Rahim Haqparast were subsequently released. However, Mihemed Hekîmpûr, Mistefa Qadirî, Mihemedsalih Husênî, Husên Ebdulahî, and Xalid Rehemî remain in detention, and their whereabouts and fate are unknown.




It was reported that all the mountaineers had been subjected to torture while in detention. The report also stated that those whose fate remains unknown have been denied the right to meet with their families and lawyers.

title: Rape case in Siverek highlighted at "Women, Justice and Memory" vigil
content:
Organised by the Amed Network Against Violence, the vigil continued for its third week outside Diyarbakır Courthouse. Participants carried photographs of women and chanted slogans including “Femicide is political,” “Protect, exonerate, prosecute” and “Jin, jiyan, azadî” (Woman, life, freedom).




Berfin Elçi, a member of the executive board of the Amed branch of the Human Rights Association (IHD), stated that femicides are not isolated incidents, but are the result of a male-dominated system, impunity and the mentality that seeks to control women’s lives.




Emphasising that women should not have to seek justice only after they have been killed, Berfin Elçi called for reports of violence to be taken seriously, suspicious deaths of women to be effectively investigated, and protection obligations to be fulfilled.




Drawing attention to the release of three defendants in the rape case in Siverek (Sêwereg), as well as the acquittal of the perpetrator tried on abuse charges despite Fatmanur Çelik’s pursuit of justice, Berfin Elçi stated that practices of impunity threaten women’s right to life.




Stories of murdered women were read aloud




During the vigil, the stories of Canan Yıldırım, Naz Aslan, Ebru Serep and Pınar Güneş, who died in different cities in October, were shared. It was reported that Canan Yıldırım was killed by the man she lived with in Antalya, while Naz As

title: Italian politicians call for Abdullah Öcalan’s freedom
content:
Politicians in Italy have stressed that the peace process between the Turkish government and the Kurdish people must advance through concrete steps, calling for Abdullah Öcalan’s freedom.




Speaking at a press conference on the peace process in Turkey, held on 20 October at Montecitorio in Rome, Movimento 5 Stelle MP Stefania Ascari said that the Kurdish people’s rights to preserve their language and culture, elect their representatives and determine their own future must be recognised.




Emphasising that these rights are universal for both Kurds and Palestinians, Ascari said that the peace process must not remain limited to statements alone.







 







Ascari: We support the process




Ascari said: “We support the peace process in Turkey and call for Abdullah Öcalan’s freedom. We want this both to ensure respect for his rights and to enable him to contribute to dialogue.”




Stating that the way must be opened for actors capable of conducting negotiations if a political solution is to be achieved, Ascari also called on the Italian government to act. She asked the government to explain what initiatives it would undertake to support the peace process and what demands it would raise regarding Abdullah Öcalan’s freedom and the rights of the Kurdish people in Turkey.

title: Bakırhan: There is no longer any justification for waiting, concrete steps must be taken
content:
Speaking at his party’s parliamentary group meeting, DEM Party Co-Chair Tuncer Bakırhan reflected on the meetings he held at the MERI Forum, organised in the Federated Kurdistan Region.




Bakırhan said they had met with Neçirvan Barzani, Bafil Talabani, Kubat Talabani, Mazlum Ebdî and İlham Ehmed at the forum, adding that Kurdish political actors attached importance to developing dialogue and to the ongoing process in Turkey.




A photograph is not enough




Bakırhan said: “Coming together and appearing side by side in a photograph is important. These meetings and photographs help close the distance that has emerged over the years, but a photograph is not enough; this rapprochement must also have political, social and diplomatic dimensions.”




The process is the hope of the entire region




Bakırhan drew attention to the ongoing political and social crises alongside wars in the Middle East, and said developments in the region were not confined to the countries directly involved, but also had economic and political consequences for other countries.




Bakırhan added that everyone in the region was seeking security, yet insufficient steps were being taken to establish genuine peace. title: The universal flow of our ancient culture
content:
We have spent the past several days attending the Jineolojî Conference alongside more than a hundred women comrades. It was exciting to see women from different regions and cultures come together through Jineolojî. Sharing Jineological experiences developed across every sphere of life was also enlightening, instructive and eye-opening.




I asked myself what this synergistic energy was that brought together women from different parts of the world. It was also heartening to see that many of them knew Kurdish and spoke it fluently. More than simply speaking the language, they regarded Kurdish as the language of free life, a language of relationships, consciousness and emotion. Perhaps this is the universal flow of our ancient culture: the archaic essence, the roots, flowing through different bodies, revealing the goodness and beauty of existence.




We live in an age in which meaning and feeling are increasingly eroding, or rather, being deliberately stripped of their value. Instead of the heartbeat, greenery, water and breath of life, we are trapped in an endless obsession with scrolling, wasting time with every swipe. This is turning individuals and society into robots day by day, destroying our ability to read, concentrate and create meaning, values and emotions. title: KNK Women’s Commission: The Iranian regime will not be able to stop Kurdish women
content:
The Women’s Commission of the Kurdistan National Congress (KNK) issued a written statement concerning the Iranian regime’s escalating repression of Kurds and its policy of executions.




Drawing attention to the growing threats and attacks against Kurds and opposition figures, as well as the ongoing repression of Kurdish women, the Commission stated that the death sentence imposed on Varisheh Moradi for a second time and the treatment of Zeynab Jalalian, who has been imprisoned for 18 years, demonstrate the regime’s fear of Kurdish women’s capacity to organise and mobilise.




Stating that the Iranian regime fears popular uprisings, the KNK Women’s Commission emphasised that the experience created by the “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” (Woman, Life, Freedom) movement has not yet been forgotten. The statement recalled that the death sentence imposed on Varisheh Moradi in November 2024 was overturned by a court in 2025, but that it was announced on 14 October 2026 that the death sentence had been reinstated.




The regime is targeting Kurdish women en particular




Stating that the Iranian regime’s actions demonstrate its hostility towards women, particularly Kurdish women, the KNK Women’s Commission noted that threats and repression would not force Kurdish women to abandon their struggle. title: Kobanê Museum becomes shelter for displaced residents
content:
Following the historic resistance in Kobanê, 70 percent of the city was completely destroyed. Part of Kobanê was left as it was, preserved as a museum for future generations: houses reduced to rubble and rooms without doors or windows.




Today, those ruins have become a shelter for many families. Displaced residents have been forced to move to Kobanê and settle there. Many of them come from Girê Spî, Raqqa and other areas from which people have been displaced. For years, these residents have been living among the ruins, holding on to the hope that one day they will return to their homes.







 







They have no choice but to live among the rubble in order to survive. Displaced residents living in the Kobanê Museum spoke to ANF about their hopes and desire to return.




A woman named Emîne Casim Qadir explained that they had been forced to leave Girê Spî eight years ago. She recounted their experience in the following words:




“When we left Girê Spî, we had to move to schools in the Xerabhişkê area. Later, we were told that there was a camp in the Til El Semin area, near Eyn Îsa, for people coming from Girê Spî, so we stayed in those tents. In summer, we lived in the scorching heat inside the tents; in winter, we endured the cold and rain.




“More recently, my husband, my children and I had to set out on the road once again, and we came to Kobanê. At first, we stayed

author: Unknown
title: YPJ remains an autonomous force in integration talks
content:
The Command of the Women’s Protection Units (YPJ) issued a statement on recent developments and the new process, declaring that “in discussions and assessments regarding the integration process, the YPJ has secured its place as an autonomous and distinct force.”




The YPJ’s statement reads as follows:




“Having a significant history and a strong stance in the fight against terrorism and the protection of humanitarian values, the Women’s Protection Units (YPJ) are informing the public, particularly our people, about recent developments and the new process. As part of efforts to establish regional stability and build a secure future, discussions and assessments regarding the integration process are ongoing. In this process, the YPJ is maintaining its place as an autonomous and distinct force.




The YPJ is not merely a military force; it is also a symbol of women’s will and labor. Therefore, comprehensive discussions are continuing regarding the details of participation and the YPJ’s role in the new structure, with the fundamental aim of preserving women’s identity, experience, and achievements. As the YPJ, we emphasize that our guiding principle at every step is to protect the achievements of our people and the legitimate rights of women. The outcomes of these discussions will be publicly announced in the coming period.”
