title: Talabani receives Bakırhan, reaffirms PUK’s support for the peace process in Turkey
content:
Bafel Jalal Talabani, President of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), received Tuncer Bakırhan, Co-Chair of the DEM Party, in Dabashan.







The meeting on Wednesday was attended by Shanaz Ibrahim Ahmed and Dr Yousif Goran, members of the PUK Political Bureau, and Salar Lala Sarhad, Head of the Kurdistani Relations Board. Discussions focused on continuing joint coordination and cooperation and strengthening bilateral relations in pursuit of shared interests and greater regional stability.







The two sides also exchanged views on the peace process in Turkey. Bafel Talabani reaffirmed the PUK’s support for this historic initiative, stating: “We will continue to follow the same policy pursued by President Mam Jalal until this vital and decisive process succeeds. We believe that peace and coexistence enable us to serve our people, whereas war and division bring nothing but destruction. I therefore hope that everyone will turn a new page and work towards lasting peace.”







For his part, Bakırhan thanked Talabani and the PUK for their efforts to advance the peace process, saying: “We highly value your role and appreciate your steps in support of stability and peaceful coexistence in the region.”







Photos: PUKMEDIA

content:

Speaking to ANF, the member of the Ticino cantonal parliament expressed serious doubts about the Turkish government’s willingness to secure the current peace process through binding political and legal guarantees. At the same time, he sees Öcalan’s concept of democratic confederalism as offering a perspective that extends beyond the Kurdish question.




Since Öcalan’s February 27, 2025, Call for Peace and Democratic Society, the Kurdish freedom movement has taken far-reaching steps toward ending the armed struggle against Turkey. According to Savary-Borioli, however, the future of this process depends crucially on whether Ankara is prepared to establish the political conditions necessary for a negotiated settlement on equal terms.

content:
Journalist Ahmed Polad, who was abducted and detained by Hayat Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) on 18 January 2026 while covering events in Syria, was handed over to Turkey on 9 September 2026 after spending eight months in HTS prisons. Polad was subsequently arrested in Turkey. His father, Adil Aslan, appealed to the public to draw attention to his son's situation.




Ahmed Polad and Eva Maria Michelmann, who had been working as journalists in Rojava for many years, were abducted on 18 January 2026 during HTS attacks on Raqqa. Following a prisoner exchange on 11 April 2026, testimonies from people held in HTS prisons revealed that both journalists were in detention.




Once their whereabouts became known, campaigns demanding their release were organised in Turkey, Kurdistan and around the world. Following public pressure, HTS handed German journalist Eva Maria Michelmann over to Germany on 18 June 2026.

content:

In a statement issued on Wednesday, the party’s leadership described the attacks on Kurdish symbols and memorial portraits of fallen women as a threat to social peace, freedom of political activity, and coexistence among the different communities in northeastern Syria.




On Tuesday, unidentified individuals forcibly entered the PYD office, broke down doors, and vandalized the premises. Kurdish symbols, particularly memorial portraits of prominent women figures of the revolution, were targeted and stolen. Images of fallen women were subsequently desecrated in public, and footage of these acts was circulated on social media. According to the authorities, a suspect has since been arrested.




Connection with attack in Til Temir




The PYD recalled that the Center of the Council of Families of Martyrs in Til Temir had also been attacked just a few days earlier. The party views these incidents as part of a deliberate campaign targeting social coexistence. “The attacks in Til Temir and now in Hesekê, as well as the destruction of our office, indicate a systematic plan aimed at undermining coexistence,” the General Council stated.

title: Provocations in Hesekê and the importance of self-defence
content:
Hesekê (al-Hasakah) is one of Syria's most diverse cities, home to Kurds, Arabs, Syriacs/Assyrians, Armenians and other communities living side by side. Kurds are concentrated mainly in the Mufti and Salihiyê neighbourhoods, while Arabs predominantly live in Xiwêran, Neşva and Tel Hacer. Different communities live together in Aziziyê and parts of the city centre.




The question of how the city is governed is directly linked to how this multi-ethnic population is represented. The Autonomous Administration model, established in Rojava and regarded as an example for the world, is based on shared governance in which different sections of society have a say. The current Syrian Interim Government in Damascus, however, advocates a return to the mentality of the Ba'ath regime. Although the 29 January Agreement initiated an integration process between Damascus and the Autonomous Administration, the current government continues to refuse to recognise the political will, identity and cultural rights of the Kurds. The murders, attacks on symbols, attempts to occupy Kurdish neighbourhoods and armed incidents witnessed in Hesekê recently have reflected this mentality in the city.

content:

EUTCC 20 years: A voice for Kurdish rights, peace and democracy




Speaking via live video link during the first session, moderated by EUTCC Board Member Dersim Dağdeviren, Kariane Westrheim thanked everyone who had contributed to the conference, saying: “When EUTCC was founded in 2004, Turkey was at an important crossroads. content:
The Freedom for Öcalan Vigil, which was launched on 25 June 2012, in Strasbourg, has entered its 746thweek.




The vigil, which continues in Strasbourg, where institutions such as the Council of Europe and the European Court of Human Rights are located, was taken over by Barış Çetin, Cihat Kalkan and Cesur Akar from Zurich.




Speaking on behalf of the demonstrators, Barış Çetin emphasized that they were protesting the conditions of isolation imposed for nearly 28 years on Abdullah Öcalan, who was imprisoned in 1999 as a result of an international conspiracy.




“We will continue until our leader’s physical freedom is secured,” Çetin said, adding, “We also want the international community to recognize the struggle taking place here and the reality of the situation. Our comrades have demonstrated their determination for 746 consecutive weeks. Our Leader’s physical freedom is of great importance to us.”




Calling on the international community to fulfill its duties and responsibilities, Çetin stated that stability and peace in the Middle East would only be possible through the freedom of Öcalan.

author: Unknown
title: YPJ Spokesperson: Any attack on the symbols of our martyrs constitutes an attack on every woman
content:
Ruksen Mohamed, spokesperson for the Women’s Protection Units (YPJ), made a statement regarding the attack that targeted the images of fallen female fighters in Hesekê.




The statement by Ruksen Mohamed reads as follows:




“In light of the recent events in Hesekê Governorate, which have witnessed acts of vandalism and grave assaults perpetrated by individuals operating outside the law, targeting the symbols and images of our fallen female martyrs, we strongly condemn and denounce these reprehensible acts, whether through tearing down their photographs, defacing them, or insulting their memory and sacrifices.




These unethical practices constitute a flagrant assault on our collective memory and conscience, as well as a violation of the humanitarian and national values embodied by our martyrs through their immense sacrifices.




Our female martyrs are symbols of struggle, dignity, and freedom. They gave their lives in defence of the land, justice, and gender equality, and their sacrifices will remain forever enshrined in the memory of our people.




We affirm that any attack on the symbols of our martyrs constitutes an attack on every woman who has struggled for freedom and legitimate rights. Such acts represent a grave moral and national offence that cannot be justified under any pretext. Accordingly, we call upon the Syrian government, represented by the Hesekê Governor

author: Unknown
title: Kongra Star holds Damascus responsible for provocations in Hesekê
content:
The Kongra Star Coordination has strongly condemned the recent attacks on Kurdish symbols and memorial portraits of fallen women in Hesekê. The women’s movement views these acts as deliberate provocations intended to fuel hostility between the Kurdish and Arab populations. It holds the Islamist transitional government in Damascus responsible for ensuring security in the city and preventing further attacks.




The statement follows an attack on an office of the Democratic Union Party (PYD) in the Xiwêran neighborhood on Tuesday. An individual entered the premises, damaged portraits of fallen women, and stole Kurdish symbols. Other memorial portraits taken from the office were subsequently desecrated in public. The perpetrator shared footage of these acts on social media. According to the ANHA news agency, the man has since been arrested by the Internal Security Forces.




Attacks target women’s struggle for freedom




Kongra Star placed the incident in the context of increasing attacks on Kurdish values, symbols, and fallen fighters since the mobilization of Arab groups from Deir ez-Zor, Raqqa, Tal Hamis, and al-Shaddadi. The women’s movement warned of attempts to divide the population along ethnic lines, saying: “Kurds, Arabs, and other communities have lived together in Hesekê for centuries. Their shared interest lies in peace and coexistence based on mutual respect, rather

author: Unknown
title: Court overturns environmental approval for Birsu hydroelectric power plant in Bingöl
content:
The Administrative Court in Bingöl has overturned the environmental approval for the planned Birsu hydroelectric power plant on the Sarim River. The judges unanimously ruled that the positive environmental impact assessment (EIA) decision was unlawful. The ruling was based on an expert report that identified significant scientific and technical deficiencies in the project’s assessment.




The hydroelectric power plant, planned by the company Silvan Elektrik Üretim, is to be built on the Sarim River in the border area between the districts of Lice and Kulp in Amed (Diyarbakır) and the district of Genç in Bingöl. Villagers have been challenging the project through legal channels for several years. They fear serious consequences for the region’s water resources, biodiversity, and agricultural livelihoods.




River flow and dry periods incorrectly assessed




According to the court, the deficiencies in calculating the available water volumes are particularly serious. The river flow data used in the project are not based on measurements taken within the affected river basin. Furthermore, the average river flow was overestimated, contradicting relevant scientific findings.




Accordingly, the pronounced dry periods between June and September were not adequately taken into account in the environmental impact assessment (EIA). As a result, there is no reliable basis for determining

author: Unknown
title: Turkish army blocks road connecting two villages in Til Temir
content:
Turkish occupation forces have blocked the only road connecting the villages of al-Manakh and al-Kanihir, north of Til Temir in northeastern Syria. Turkish soldiers stationed in al-Manakh erected earthen barriers across the road, cutting off the direct connection between the two villages.




According to the ANHA news agency, citing local sources, the Turkish military is also preventing residents from accessing their homes and agricultural land in Turkish-occupied areas.

author: Unknown
title: Diyarbakır City Hospital workers demand their rights
content:
Construction workers at the Diyarbakır (Amed) City Hospital construction site, where work began in November 2021, have been subjected to systematic pressure for years. The workers previously staged two protests over unpaid wages and difficult working conditions. Most recently, they launched another protest against dismissals linked to their union membership. The protest, organised by 75 members of the Construction and Road Workers' Union (Yapı Yol-Sen) demanding improved working conditions and the recognition of their employment rights, has continued for 14 days.







 







The workers have continued their protest with traditional halay dances, demanding an end to unfair wage deductions, the underpayment of Social Security Institution (SGK) contributions based on wages lower than their actual earnings, unpaid overtime and Sunday work, and problems concerning travel allowances and workplace safety. They said they faced pressure, threats and the risk of dismissal for exercising their trade union rights and vowed to continue their struggle until their demands were met.




‘We faced workplace bullying because of our union membership’




Yapı Yol-Sen member Mehmet Yariç said that all workers at the construction site, not only union members, were under pressure and that working conditions were deteriorating by the day.




Yariç said: “We were constantly under pressure at work

author: Unknown
title: Release of two prisoners postponed again
content:
The release of Zeliha Ustabaş, who is held at Sincan Women’s Closed Prison, has been blocked for the fifth time by a decision of the Prison Administration and Observation Board.




Ustabaş’s release, which has been postponed four times since 18 July 2024, has now been delayed by a further nine months.




It was reported that Ustabaş’s current sentence period is due to end on 24 July 2027, and that 8 July 2027 has been set as the date for a reassessment of her case.




The release of Orhan Yakışır, who is held at Sincan No. 1 High-Security Prison, has also been postponed, for the third time.




Yakışır’s release was previously postponed by three months on the first occasion and eight months on the second. His release has now been delayed by a further 11 months.




It was stated that the board’s next review of Yakışır’s case will take place on 7 September 2027.

author: Unknown
title: Gülsüm Elvan: Peace requires justice and women's struggle
content:
Eighty women from the women's movement, politics, academia, culture and the arts came together on 21 September under the appeal “Side by Side, Talking About the Future”, declaring that resolving the Kurdish question through democratic politics and negotiations would mark a new era for democracy in Turkey.




Gülsüm Elvan, the mother of Berkin Elvan, who was struck by a police-fired tear gas canister during the Gezi Resistance and died at the age of 15 after spending nine months in a coma, spoke to ANF about why she signed the appeal and what peace means for women.




‘Let no more mothers weep, let no more children be killed’




Gülsüm Elvan explained her reasons for signing the appeal, stressing her pursuit of justice and her determination to prevent other families from experiencing the same suffering. Elvan said: “The reason I signed this appeal is clear. I am a mother whose heart has been broken, whose child was taken from her, who has sought justice but has never been able to find it. At the same time, throughout my struggle for justice, whenever I speak about Berkin, I have always said, ‘Let no more mothers weep, let no more children be killed.’”




‘We will bring peace through struggle, women are rising up’




Elvan said that, as a mother who had lost her child, she believed genuine peace meant defending life. She drew attention to femicides and the deepening cycle of

author: Unknown
title: Iranian mountaineer and musician Ali-Sina Mustafavi executed
content:
According to Mizan News Agency, affiliated with Iran’s judiciary, Ali-Sina Mustafavi, a 38-year-old from Kerman, was executed on Wednesday. Human rights organisations had warned a day before the execution that it could be imminent after Mustafavi was placed in solitary confinement. Prison authorities were reportedly in contact with his family and had summoned them for a final visit.




Human Rights for Sports, an organisation that advocates for athletes’ rights, had also included Mustafavi, a mountaineer and musician, on its list of athletes at risk of execution. Human rights organisations said that Mustafavi had been forced to confess.




Mizan News Agency accused Mustafavi of carrying out armed attacks in Kerman in which civilians were injured. The report alleged that the attacks were carried out in support of Iran’s Crown Prince Reza Pahlavi and Israel.




Mizan also claimed that Mustafavi had filmed areas that were struck during the war. However, the agency provided no details about the trial proceedings or the evidence presented in court.




Iranian authorities systematically and arbitrarily use charges such as espionage, crimes against national security, armed rebellion, “enmity against God” and “corruption on earth” to prosecute dissidents and protesters. author: Unknown
title: Xebat Kobanê: A war veteran devoted to music and song
content:
Every war veteran who has sacrificed part of their body to protect their land and people in North and East Syria has a different story. Xebat Kobanê is one of them.




Xebat grew up in a patriotic family. One of his brothers was martyred, while one of his sisters joined the ranks of the revolution.







 







Xebat joined the People's Protection Units (YPG) with great enthusiasm and hope. He stood on the front lines of resistance in many areas against treacherous attacks targeting his land and people.




Xebat knew that martyrdom and injury were possibilities on this honourable path. Alongside his military training, he also developed himself ideologically. Conscious of following in the footsteps of Arîn and Rêvan, he took on all aspects of revolutionary work with great dedication.




Xebat Kobanê was wounded during a period of intense fighting, leaving both his legs paralysed. However, he has never regarded his injury as an obstacle. He follows Abdullah Öcalan's perspectives on war veterans and acts on the principle that “veterans are defenders of the revolution”.




Xebat has been interested in music for many years and plays the saz, a traditional long-necked string instrument, with remarkable skill. He also has a beautiful singing voice.




War veteran Xebat Kobanê takes his saz wherever he goes. He plays and sings songs for his fellow war veterans.

author: Unknown
title: Martyr Welat wanted to be the voice of truth
content:
The early days of the Rojava Revolution saw many people living in Rojava seeking to become the voice of their society and expose the attacks, violations and suffering endured by their people. However, this was no easy task. Journalists who decided to document the realities faced by the people encountered numerous difficulties and dangers. Many lost their lives in pursuit of this mission. Many journalists seeking to document the atrocities committed during the Turkish state's occupation attacks on North and East Syria were targeted, particularly during the attacks on Serêkaniyê and Girê Spî in October 2019. One of them was martyr Vedat (Welat) Erdemci, who remained determined to be the voice of his people and bring the truth about the region to public attention until his final moments.




Journalist Zinar Cafer spoke to ANF about the life and work of journalist Vedat Erdemci, who was martyred during the attacks on Serêkaniyê on 11 October 2019.







Cafer said that a few words could never adequately convey the stories of the martyrs of the free press and added: “Writing books about the martyrs of the press or speaking about them in programmes is not enough on its own. At the beginning of the Rojava Revolution, many people in Kurdistan wanted to become the voice of their society because we witnessed numerous violations and attacks. The Rojava region of Kurdistan was experienci

author: Unknown
title: Two Iraqi soldiers killed in mine explosion in Kirkuk
content:
An officer and a soldier from the Iraqi army were killed in a mine explosion in Kirkuk on Wednesday. Two other soldiers were injured. The explosion occurred in Wadi Zixêtûn (Zghaitoun), near Reşad (Rashad), when a military vehicle belonging to the 11th Division triggered a previously planted mine.




Among those killed was Ahat Yasir, the division’s communications officer. The unit had been deployed to the area to investigate suspected positions and activities of remaining militants from the terrorist organization Islamic State (ISIS).




The previous day, the Iraqi Air Force had carried out airstrikes on ISIS positions in the valley south of Kirkuk. The soldiers involved had subsequently been dispatched on a reconnaissance mission.

author: Unknown
title: YPJ: Attack on the images of our martyrs is an assault on the honour and values of our society
content:
The General Command of the Women’s Protection Units (YPJ) released a statement condemning the attacks against the images of fallen female fighters in Hesekê.




The YPJ statement on Wednesday said: “Recently, despicable attempts and attacks have targeted images of our martyrs and the sanctity they represent, which are among the most sacred values of our people and our revolution. These attacks, which directly target the dignity of our martyrs, violate the fundamental principles of humanity, moral awareness, and the inviolable red lines of society’s conscience.”




The statement stressed that: “Our martyrs are our identity, our honour, and the most sacred values underpinning our existence. Those who were defeated by the will and resistance of free women are now attacking our martyrs through inhumane methods that go beyond all standards of human morality. These immoral scenes and despicable acts are in no way befitting our people or our homeland. Such attacks constitute a direct assault on the honour and values of our entire society.”




The YPJ General Command called on the Damascus government to assume its responsibility, take immediate action against these inhumane acts, and hold those responsible fully accountable to the fullest extent possible. YPJ vowed that: “We will not remain silent in the face of these attacks, and no violation of the sanctity of our martyrs will go

author: Unknown
title: Families condemn the attack on the images of martyrs: We will continue on the path of our martyrs
content:
Rojin Mohammad, a founding member of the Martyrs’ Families Foundation in Kobanê, expressed her dismay at the attacks targeting images of martyrs in Hesekê, stating, “We will not accept such immoral acts.”




Rojin Mohammad explained that, for several days, certain groups have been systematically spreading chaos in the al-Khuwairan neighbourhood of Hesekê and attacking images of the martyrs.




“This is an attack on all peoples”




Speaking about the attacks, Rojin Mohammad said: “These martyrs sacrificed their lives for the freedom of Syrian soil and to protect all peoples from massacres. Attacking their images is not an attack on their families alone; it is an attack on all our values. This is a clear violation of the law.”




“The aim is to derail the integration process”




Mohammad pointed out that the aim of these attacks is to undermine the integration process in Syria. She continued: “This chaos and recklessness will not allow Syria to achieve integration or reach a positive outcome. On the contrary, these acts are an attempt to obstruct the integration process. The Syrian state must take notice of these attacks, put an end to these acts of sabotage, and hold those responsible accountable.”




“We will continue on their path”




Rojin Mohammad concluded her message by saying: “A democratic and free Syria must be built through the joint efforts of all its component

author: Unknown
title: Aynur Sarıca: Women must play a founding role in the peace process
content:
Aynur Sarıca of the Jineolojî Academy drew attention to the role women must play in the Peace and Democratic Society Process, saying that pressure and attacks against the women's movement in Kurdistan were continuing.




Sarıca said women must not be confined to following the process or being represented on monitoring commissions, stressing that their participation in decision-making mechanisms was crucial to building a democratic society.




Sarıca said women had played an important role in shaping social life throughout history, but that the nation-state mentality and patriarchal structures continued to attack women's labour, identity and lives. She added that women's historical role had been pushed into the background in dominant narratives.







 







Sarıca said women had often been treated as spoils of war or as instruments for ensuring the continuation of a lineage during periods of war and conflict, but had fought throughout history to defend their existence against such attacks.




She said attacks on women's identity, children, labour and social life had continued through different methods as conflicts intensified in Kurdistan. She added that operations and detentions targeting the women's movement were intended to prevent the struggle for women's freedom from taking root throughout society.




Sarıca said: “Women have asserted their struggle for existence in

author: Unknown
title: Peace Mothers join 'Tuesdays Against Executions' campaign
content:
The Kurdistan Peace Mothers issued a statement regarding their participation in the 'Sêşema Na ji bo Darvekirinê' ('Tuesdays Against Executions') campaign.




The statement drew attention to how Iran’s regime, through its unfair courts, sentences political prisoners and civilians to mass executions every day on baseless charges. It said: “With each passing day, the shadow of the executioner regime weighs more heavily on prisoners.”




Emphasizing that life, freedom, and human dignity are fundamental and inalienable rights, the statement stressed that no mother should be forced to live in fear of her child being executed. It continued: “Execution does not merely bring one person’s life to an end; it also condemns a family to suffer forever. An execution leaves a profound impact on a family for the rest of its life. We offer our support to families who have lost their loved ones.




We demand that the fate of the prisoners be clarified as soon as possible. We call on all families, human rights organizations, and defenders of freedom to be the voice of the prisoners until freedom is secured, and the truth comes to light.”

author: Unknown
title: Police raid Halk TV: broadcast suspended, trustee appointed
content:
Police raided Halk TV’s headquarters in Istanbul in the early hours of Wednesday morning. A trustee was appointed, and its television broadcast was halted. While police searches of the building continued, the road where the channel is located was closed to traffic, and employees were denied entry to the building.




Reporting on the latest developments inside the building after police entered Halk TV, channel presenter Deniz Bayramoğlu said: “Halk TV Editor-in-Chief Suat Toktaş held talks with the head of the trustee board about continuing the broadcast, but the talks were inconclusive. The broadcast has been suspended.”




As part of the investigation, arrest warrants were issued for 17 people, and 11 people were reportedly taken into custody.




Halk TV Board Chair Cafer Mahiroğlu also announced the police raid on social media. Mahiroğlu said: “Kılıçdaroğlu, the leader of the annulment faction, and his team may be happy. The police are at Halk TV.”




Press organisations and unions protest the attack on press freedom




The appointment of a trustee to Halk TV and the suspension of its broadcast prompted protests from press organisations and journalists’ unions. DISK Basın-Iş, the Contemporary Journalists’ Association (ÇGD), and the Journalists’ Union of Turkey (TGS) condemned the decision as interference in press and freedom of expression.




DİSK Basın-Iş stated that t

author: Unknown
title: Ecological destruction in the Zilan Valley continues
content:
Construction work on an irrigation canal in the Zilan Valley (Geliyê Zîlan), near the district of Erciş in Van province, is causing increasing damage to the region’s ecosystem. Since September 23, heavy construction machinery has been operating in the canyon as part of the so-called Pay Irrigation Canal Project. Excavation and construction work in the streambed and surrounding areas have altered the natural flow of water. Water levels have dropped significantly, and some sections of the stream have already dried up.




These developments threaten not only to have serious consequences for local wildlife and vegetation but also to exacerbate water supply problems in the region. Environmental activists have initiated legal proceedings against the project and requested a suspension of construction work. A court decision is still pending, while machinery continues operating in the valley.




Trees felled and riverside vegetation destroyed




The areas along the streambanks have been particularly severely affected. Trees have been felled and large sections of natural vegetation cleared within the valley. The grasses, shrubs, and trees growing in the area perform essential functions in maintaining the ecological balance: they stabilize the soil, prevent erosion, regulate water levels, and provide habitats for numerous animal species.

author: Unknown
title: Kurdish literature and cultural memory meet at Frankfurt Book Fair
content:
The 78th Frankfurt International Book Fair, which opened on 7 October in Frankfurt, Germany, concluded on Sunday evening, 11 October. The fair brought together publishing houses, writers, cultural institutions, journalists, academics and representatives of the publishing industry from around the world.




A total of 4,131 exhibitors participated in the fair, which hosted more than 3,600 events.




As one of the international meeting points for the book and publishing industry, the fair also provided a platform for discussions on literature, culture, freedom of expression, democracy, human rights and the future of technology.




‘Czechia was the guest of honour’




Czechia was this year's guest of honour at the Frankfurt Book Fair.




Under the theme “Ein Land an der Küste” (A Country on the Coast), Czechia established a 2,300-square-metre exhibition space at the fair. The Guest of Honour Pavilion hosted events covering various literary genres, with the participation of 75 writers.




The pavilion showcased Czech literature and the country's cultural heritage, incorporating artificial intelligence and interactive technologies. Visitors engaged with digital installations, while a live-drawing robot and interactive poetry applications attracted particular attention.




More than 40 publishing houses took part in Czechia's national presentation, showcasing their books and ho

author: Unknown
title: Tosun: The case is not over until the third attacker is punished
content:
One year has passed since journalist, documentary filmmaker and environmental activist Hakan Tosun was beaten to death in the street in Esenyurt.




Tosun died after suffering a brain haemorrhage at the scene when he was assaulted by two people on the night of 10–11 October 2025 while on his way to visit his mother in the Mehmet Akif Ersoy neighbourhood of Esenyurt district.




Abdurrahman Murat and Adnan Şahin, responsible for Hakan Tosun's death, were summoned to the Esenyurt Mevlana Police Station to give statements and were arrested on charges of intentional injury. However, it was notable that Yusuf Özakdağ, a third person who had also participated in the attack, was questioned as a witness by the same police station.




Although a report by the Council of Forensic Medicine confirmed that Hakan Tosun had been severely beaten, the 17th High Criminal Court accepted the indictment for intentional injury prepared by the Büyükçekmece Chief Public Prosecutor's Office. Following months of proceedings, Abdurrahman Murat and Adnan Şahin were sentenced to life imprisonment for intentional killing. However, the verdict brought no sense of relief to the Tosun family.




Hakan Tosun's sister, Öznur Tosun, spoke to ANF and stressed that the case would not be over until Yusuf Özakdağ, who also participated in the fatal attack on her brother and has openly posed with firearms on socia

author: Unknown
title: BaBa Zula: We stand for peace, the government must act
content:
Artists continue to share messages of peace through ANF. Members of the music group BaBa Zula said artists should take a political stance and called for Kurdish and all other languages spoken in the country to be free.




The musicians said: “The Justice and Development Party (AKP) does not inspire confidence. For peace to come, democracy, rights and the rule of law must come first. Thousands of our people from Anatolia and Mesopotamia have lost their lives. Peace is not a concession granted from above or a political favour. It means people being able to live freely, with their fundamental rights, mother tongues and cultures protected under a fair legal system.”




Murat Ertel, Esma Ertel and Levent Akman of the music group BaBa Zula answered ANF's questions.




‘Artists are being prevented from taking political positions’




Members of BaBa Zula said the group seeks to preserve the multicultural and multilingual heritage of Anatolia, Mesopotamia and Istanbul through its music. They said: “We are living under a cultural bombardment. There is a situation being created, particularly in the virtual world. It is as though the world is being shaped not by its seven billion people, but by the leaders of a population of just one billion. They are also trying to shape culture, but we are interested in the culture of the geography we live in. We eat the food of this region, listen t

author: Unknown
title: The people of Shengal must decide their own future
content:
More than 6,000 people were abducted during the attack on Shengal by ISIS mercenaries on 3 August 2014, and around 2,500 remain missing. The Yazidis refer to the attack, in which thousands of people were massacred and abducted, as the 74th Ferman in their history.




Shengal was liberated from ISIS in 2015. In the aftermath of the Ferman (Shengal genocide), the Yazidis established their own administrative and defence mechanisms, forming a People's Council and defence forces such as the Shengal Resistance Units (YBŞ) and Shengal Women's Units (YJŞ). The autonomous administration, which has operated in practice in Shengal ever since, continues to exist as an expression of the people's determination to govern and defend themselves.




Turkey-Iraq trade-off in New York




Turkish President Tayyip Erdoğan and Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Zeydi met in New York on 23 September 2026 while attending the United Nations (UN) General Assembly. The joint statement issued after the meeting highlighted two main points: the full restoration of state authority in Shengal and the elimination of forces described in the statement as “prohibited foreign armed elements”, and the gradual transfer of the Turkish army's Bashiqa (Zilkan) base to the Iraqi federal government. The transfer process was made conditional on security measures to be taken by Iraq and a timetable to be agreed upon by both sides.

author: Unknown
title: PACE delegation meets with the DEM Party in Ankara, discusses the peace process
content:
Petra Bayr, President of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE), held talks with the DEM Party during her official visit to Turkey on Monday. Accompanied by her delegation, she met with Co-Chair Tülay Hatimoğulları, Deputy Parliamentary Group Chair Sezai Temelli, and MP Sevilay Çelenk, who is a member of the Turkish delegation to PACE, at the Turkish Parliament.




The discussions focused on the role of Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan in the Peace and Democratic Society Process. Reference was made to the case law of the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) concerning the so-called “right to hope.” DEM Party representatives emphasized that Öcalan must be provided with living and working conditions that would allow him to participate freely in the peace process.




The discussions also addressed the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) rulings concerning imprisoned politicians Selahattin Demirtaş and Figen Yüksekdağ, as well as human rights activist and cultural philanthropist Osman Kavala, which have yet to be implemented. The Council of Europe delegation expressed its concern regarding these issues. Further meetings with political representatives in Turkey are scheduled as part of the official visit.

author: Unknown
title: ‘Women, Justice and Memory Vigil’ against femicides in its second week
content:
The Amed (tr: Diyarbakır) Network for Combating Violence launched a “Women, Justice and Memory Vigil” against femicides and suspicious deaths of women last Tuesday, October 6. The vigil outside the Diyarbakır Courthouse will continue at the same location every Tuesday for 10 weeks.




Participants displayed a banner reading “Women Hold a Vigil for Justice and Memory,” along with photographs of women who had been killed.  Representatives of numerous political parties and civil society organizations attended the vigil in its second week.




Reading the statement on behalf of the Rosa Women’s Association, Ruşen Yakut said that during this week’s vigil, they were bringing together in collective memory the stories of women who were killed in different cities across Turkey between October 2 and 12 and whose information they had been able to obtain.




Emphasizing that the struggle for justice for murdered women is not limited to any particular period, Yakut stated that they would never abandon their demand for truth and justice. “For us, memory means remembering, leaving a trace, and ensuring that these women are not forgotten. The pursuit of justice means carrying the collective responsibility to protect women’s right to life into the present,” she said.




Following the statement, the stories of Füsun Yuluğkural, Gözde Çelik, Emel Bozkuş, Fadime Akbal, Gülşah Oktay, Sakine Y, F

author: Unknown
title: Kurdish women’s movement participates in 39th Plurinational Gathering of Women in Argentina
content:
The 39th Plurinational Gathering of Women and Gender-Diverse People, held in Córdoba, Argentina from October 10 to 12, brought together hundreds of thousands of women from across Latin America. Organized by 300 local organizations, the gathering featured workshops, panel discussions, film screenings, and meetings.







 








A delegation from the Kurdish women’s movement participated in a meeting on internationalism, organized jointly with the Abya Yala feminist network, a panel titled “Revolutionary Practices,” and a screening of the film 

In Search of Alina

. The events addressed the experiences of Kurdish women, the women’s revolution in Rojava, the struggle of women guerrillas in the mountains of Kurdistan, and the importance of international solidarity.




At the meeting on internationalism organized by the Kurdish women’s movement and the Abya Yala feminist network, discussions focused on the international dimension of Kurdish women’s struggle and the importance of the “Women Weaving the Future” network. Participants chanted the slogan, “Plurinational, plurinational; from Abya Yala to Kurdistan!”




During the panel titled “Revolutionary Practices,” the delegation spoke about the women’s revolution in Rojava, the struggle of women guerrillas in Kurdistan, and the role of internationalism. Following questions from participants, the delegation also addressed the P

author: Unknown
title: Conditions that gave rise to the Kurdish question and the conflict remain unchanged
content:
The conflict between the Turkish state and the PKK has been at a standstill for two years. The PKK has dissolved itself and decided to end its armed struggle against Turkey. The PKK disbanded and took significant steps in 2025 and 2026. All these steps were taken to enable free and unrestricted participation in democratic politics and to achieve a democratic resolution to the Kurdish question.




From the statement issued by the Kurdish Movement Leadership on October 8, we learn that the Turkish state has taken no steps apart from allowing meetings on Imralı Island every few months. More precisely, the Movement Leadership has conveyed this reality, which we have also witnessed, in the form of a polite warning. The statement emphasized that there is no longer any justification for the Turkish state’s failure to act following the significant steps taken by the movement.




The Movement Leadership stated that their leader must be freed and that legislation on freedoms, which would pave the way for a democratic resolution to the Kurdish question, must be enacted without delay. They specifically emphasized that if the Turkish state fails to take steps demonstrating such political will, they will interpret this as an intention to continue its previous policies.




The Movement Leadership made it clear that if the Turkish state takes no action and instead continues to demand furthe

author: Unknown
title: A new chapter in the heart of Paris: Kurdistan House of France
content:
The Kurdistan House of France, which aims to bring together the cultural, social, academic, and institutional activities of the Kurdish community in France under one roof, was officially unveiled to the public at a grand ceremony held at Paris City Hall.




The event, held on the evening of Monday, October 12, in the historic hall of Paris City Hall, located in the political and historical heart of the French capital, brought together politicians, institutional representatives, artists, academics, association leaders, and civil society figures from the Kurdish and French communities.




Three speeches were delivered during the evening. Paris Mayor Emmanuel Grégoire gave the opening address, followed by Baran Gürbüz, President of the Kurdistan House of France. Former French President François Hollande delivered the final political address of the evening.




Official launch at historic Paris City Hall




The decision to hold the official launch of the Kurdistan House of France (Maison du Kurdistan de France) at Paris City Hall itself was one of the evening’s most significant symbolic and political messages.
